sections.h2: What does the Shiawassee County Register of Deeds do?
sections.html:
The Shiawassee County Register of Deeds is the county's official repository for deeds, land contracts, mortgages and other real estate records. It checks each document against the recording statute, numbers and times it, indexes it and keeps the original images safe. Proof of ownership in the county rests on what this office has on record.

Michigan's first constitution in 1835 set up the Register of Deeds as the recording office in each county. Shiawassee's own records start in 1836, a year before the county was established in 1837. From 1954 forward the records are scanned and indexed in the computer system, and the office says all of them can be searched by liber and page. The office is in the Circuit Courthouse at 208 N. Shiawassee Street, first floor, Corunna, MI 48817, phone 989-743-2216, email rod@shiawassee.net.

sections.h2: When is the Shiawassee County Register of Deeds open?
sections.html:
The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to noon and from 1:05 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. The search room keeps slightly shorter hours, 8:15 to 11:45 a.m. and 1:05 to 4:45 p.m. The county's holiday schedule page asks visitors to call and arrange an appointment, so phone ahead if you are bringing a closing package.

The office accepts cash and checks payable to the Register of Deeds for recording charges. Card payments are available for copies and search fees, and a $1.00 convenience fee is added when you print from the website.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a deed in Shiawassee County?
sections.html:
Recording a deed is $30.00 per document. A warranty deed, land contract, land contract assignment or condominium master deed also needs a $5.00 tax certificate from the county treasurer, a requirement that comes from MCL 211.135. The treasurer's office is on the second floor of the same courthouse, phone 989-743-2224.

sections.h2: How is the Michigan transfer tax figured in Shiawassee County?
sections.html:
Shiawassee County collects two taxes at recording under MCL 207.505 (the county tax) and MCL 207.526 (the state tax). The county's schedule prints the rates as .0075 for the state and .0011 for the county, applied to the sale price, and lists the result in $500 steps. The first row covers sales from $100.00 to $500, at $3.75 state and $0.55 county.

The county's schedule adds several points a seller should know:

  • The tax falls on the seller, the grantor on the deed.
  • The deed must state the total consideration on its face, along with any exemption claimed.
  • A parcel that lies in more than one county is split, with each county taxing its share of the price.
  • Documentary stamps can be bought only in the county where the property sits.
  • A Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit can be filed with no fee, if the deed says it is being filed.

sections.h2: Which transfers are exempt from the county transfer tax?
sections.html:
The county posts the exemption list from MCL 207.505. Among the exempt items are instruments where the consideration is under $100, instruments given as security and their discharges, leases, and conveyances by a husband or wife that create or end a tenancy by the entireties. Court judgments and orders are exempt unless a specific monetary consideration is ordered.

Two exemptions come up often in family transfers: a quitclaim deed used only to correct a flaw in title, and an instrument creating a joint tenancy where at least one of the people already owned the property. A land contract is exempt while legal title stays with the seller until the full price is paid. The county also posts a separate page on the state exemption, so ask the office which statute section to cite on your deed.

sections.h2: What makes a Shiawassee County deed recordable?
sections.html:
The office posts an excerpt of Act 103 of 1937 (MCL 565.201). It turns away deeds that fail any of these tests:

  • Each signer's name is printed or typed under the signature, in black or dark blue ink, and matches the acknowledgment.
  • The grantee's street or post office address appears on the deed.
  • The first page has a 2.5 inch unprinted top margin, other margins are at least half an inch, and type is 10 point or larger.
  • The first line of print on page one identifies the recordable event, and the instrument evidences only one.
  • The first five digits of any Social Security number are removed.
  • The deed carries the drafter's name and business address, and a written English translation is attached to any foreign-language part.

The office requires the original document with original signatures. A deed for unplatted land must also include the right-to-farm statement from MCL 560.109, which tells buyers that nearby farms may produce noise, dust and odors. A surviving spouse records a certified death certificate; no new deed is issued, because the office is only a recording office.

sections.h2: What else does Shiawassee County list for sellers and buyers?
sections.html:
Sheriff's sales are held on Wednesday mornings at 10:00 a.m. in the lobby of the 35th Circuit Court at 208 N. Shiawassee Street, and a certified check for the full opening bid is required. The Register of Deeds page also links a property fraud alert service. County Equalization, phone 989-743-2263, advises the Board of Commissioners on assessments across the county's 21 units of local government and can answer questions on ownership, valuation, millage rates and exemption status.

Shiawassee County covers 541 square miles in central Michigan. The Shiawassee River passes through Corunna, the county seat, and Owosso, the largest city. The other cities are Durand, Laingsburg, Perry and part of Ovid. I-69 crosses the southwest and exits east near Durand, which has an Amtrak station on the Blue Water route, while M-21 runs through Corunna and Owosso. Michigan's population center was located in Bennington Township in 2010.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Shiawassee County housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimated 67,681 residents on July 1, 2025, down from 70,648 in 2010, with 22.2 percent aged 65 or older. The county had 30,484 housing units and 28,126 households in the 2020 through 2024 period, and 80.1 percent of homes were owner-occupied. Building permits totaled 71 in 2025.

The median owner-occupied home is valued at $171,600, median rent is $899 and median household income is $67,404. The Census Bureau puts mean travel time to work at 27.8 minutes, and the county has only 128 people per square mile, so most parcels are not on a city grid.

faqs.q: How much does the Shiawassee County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: It charges $30.00 per document. Warranty deeds and land contracts need an additional $5.00 tax certificate from the county treasurer, and the state and county transfer taxes are collected on the sale price at recording.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on a sale in Shiawassee County?
faqs.a: The seller pays it. The county's tax schedule says the tax falls on the seller or grantor, with the state rate at .0075 and the county rate at .0011 of the sale price.

faqs.q: Can I record a copy of my deed in Shiawassee County?
faqs.a: No. The office needs the original document with original signatures. Anyone can get a copy of a recorded deed afterward for $1.00 per page, or $5.00 more to certify it.

faqs.q: Does the register of deeds issue a new deed when a spouse dies?
faqs.a: No. Bring a certified death certificate and the recording fee, and the office records it to show the deceased owner no longer holds an interest. The original deed remains your deed.

faqs.q: Where is the Shiawassee County Register of Deeds located?
faqs.a: It is in the Circuit Courthouse at 208 N. Shiawassee Street, first floor, Corunna, Michigan 48817. Call 989-743-2216 before you go, since the county's holiday page asks visitors to call and schedule an appointment.
